title: First-time offender leniency in NDPS - myth or reality
p1:
First offence in a drug case? Many assume the law will automatically go easy.

But under the NDPS Act, that assumption can be dangerously misleading.
p2:
A common myth is that a first-time offender always gets a lighter punishment. The reality is more nuanced.

Courts may consider factors like the quantity involved, the role of the accused, and the circumstances of the case. A first offence alone does not create an automatic right to leniency or release.
p3:
One lesser-known point: the NDPS Act treats offences involving different quantities differently. The law distinguishes between small, intermediate, and commercial quantities, and these classifications can significantly affect legal consequences.

The practical takeaway? 'First time' is only one factor, not a free pass. Each case depends on its specific facts and evidence.
conclusion: Do you think first-time offenders in serious criminal matters should receive special consideration, or should the nature of the offence matter more than past record?
